turns.said: Hello, and welcome back. Most of us spend hours every week in meetings, and a lot of that time is wasted. Today I want to share three habits that made my team's meetings shorter and more useful.
The first habit is a written agenda. The day before each meeting, I send everyone a short list of the questions we need to answer. If I can't write that list, we probably don't need the meeting.
It also means people arrive prepared. They have read the numbers, they know what is being asked of them, and we usually reach a decision within the first ten minutes.
When I began doing this, about a third of our regular meetings simply disappeared from the calendar, and nobody missed them.

turns.expected: Nothing deleted; doesn't claim it was

turns.said: The second habit is a shorter guest list. I only invite the people who make the decision or do the work. Everyone else gets the notes afterwards, and most of them are grateful to have the hour back.

The third habit is ending with names and dates. Before anyone leaves, we say out loud who is doing what, and by when. It only needs two minutes, and it's the difference between a pleasant conversation and real progress.
None of this needs new software or a bigger budget. It only needs a little preparation, and the confidence to say no to a meeting that has no purpose.
If one of these habits helps your team, let me know in the comments. Thank you for watching, and I'll see you next week.
